newsitem.title: UK: Euro low sulphur brought down by active cargo trade.
newsitem.headline: Euro low sulphur brought down by active cargo trade.

text.p: European low sulphur fuel prices were depressed on Tuesday by cargo deals and activity in paper markets, traders said.
Swaps fell $2.50 yesterday and lost a further $1 on the back of rumours of a large cargo deal into Italy at $95 cif.
The deal was subsequently denied but prices did not recover, although dealers said they stood at a small premium to May swaps levels of $84/$85.
Two smaller cargo deals were heard done and went undenied. One was from a French major with British plant who sold into Italy.
The other was from Belgium to a large trader with a requirement in the eastern Mediterranean.
Rumours that trans-atlantic shipment of one percent cracked could be made to work were discounted by most in the market late in the day.
Active low sulphur unusually left barge trade in the shade. High sulphur prices slipped slightly, with business again thin and players again complaining of manipulation.
A deal was heard done at $79.50 but the bulk of activity was in the $80-$81 range.
"It was another messy day," was all one trader would say.
A public holiday in Holland was likely to keep things quiet again on Wednesday, he added.

Cargo markets were quiet, although 70,000 tonnes of high density, high sulphur cracked was heard bought at the end of last week from Le Havre by a Swiss-based trader. Its price and end-use were not immediately known. - London newsroom +44 171 542 8060
